symbols.name: number of axes
symbols.meaning: The number of axes (coordinates) of an index.
symbols.quote: where $d$ is the number of axes.

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The even number of entries along axis i.
symbols.quote: On axis $i$, $t_i$ is the even number of entries along that axis and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

symbols.name: coprime integer
symbols.meaning: An integer coprime to t_i, scaling the frequency read along axis i.
symbols.quote: On axis $i$, $t_i$ is the even number of entries along that axis and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

symbols.name: total entries
symbols.meaning: The total number of entries, the product of the t_i.
symbols.quote: Put $T=\prod_i t_i$, the total number of entries.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The target permutation, reading frequency (-s_i j_i)_i at output position j.
symbols.quote: The permutation $Q$ is the target permutation: output position $\boldsymbol j$ reads frequency $\boldsymbol f=(-s_ij_i)_i$.

symbols.name: chirp
symbols.meaning: The chirp, a quadratic-phase array exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i).
symbols.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$, a phase quadratic in the index, and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate.

relations.quote: The Bluestein chirp identity rewrites a permuted [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) as a pointwise chirp phase, a [cyclic convolution](convolution.md), and another chirp phase, so the target permutation of resampling is absorbed into the convolution and never executed as a sort.
The permuted transform is thus reduced to one [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$ between two pointwise phase multiplications.

derivations.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$, a phase quadratic in the index, and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate.

Replacing $j_i$ by $j_i+t_i$ changes the exponent by $-\pi i s_i\frac{(j_i+t_i)^2-j_i^2}{t_i}=-\pi i s_i(2j_i+t_i)$, which is an integral multiple of $2\pi i$ because $t_i$ is even, so $a$ has period $t_i$ in coordinate $i$.

Using $(j_i-k_i)^2=j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2$, the exponent of this product is $\sum_i\frac{\pi i s_i}{t_i}\bigl(j_i^2-(j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2)+k_i^2\bigr)$, where the squares cancel, so the coefficient is $\frac1T\overline a_{\boldsymbol j}a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}\overline a_{\boldsymbol k}=\frac1T\exp(2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i)$.
This is precisely the coefficient of $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ found above, because $Q$ reads frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$ from the negative-sign transform.
